records.name: Ryusen-ji (Meguro Fudoson)
records.description: A Tendai Buddhist temple traditionally said to have been founded in 808 by the monk Ennin. It enshrines a black-eyed statue of Fudo Myoo, one of five protective Fudo statues placed around the outskirts of Edo, and gave the surrounding Meguro district its name.

tips.text: The temple's Tokko-no-taki waterfall lies within the grounds; tradition holds that the founder threw his ritual implement (tokko) here to symbolize the destruction of worldly desire.

records.name: Gohyaku Rakan-ji Temple
records.description: A Buddhist temple originally founded in 1695 in what is now Koto Ward; it relocated to Sumida in 1887 and settled at its present Meguro site in 1908. It is known for its collection of stone rakan (Buddhist arhat) statues carved by the sculptor-monk Shoun Genkei.

tips.text: Admission is ¥500 for adults (¥400 for seniors and students); free for junior-high age and younger.
Fudo-mae Station on the Tokyu Meguro Line is about an 8-minute walk; Meguro Station is about 12 minutes.

records.name: Daien-ji Temple
records.description: A Tendai Buddhist temple founded in 1624 on the historic Gyoninzaka slope, dedicated to Daikokuten and Shakyamuni. Historians believe the Great Fire of Meiwa of 1772, one of Edo's major fires, originated here; the temple's hundreds of stone rakan (Buddhist disciple) statues were carved afterward to memorialize the victims.
records.station: Meguro Station (JR Yamanote Line), about 5 minutes on foot

records.name: Yuten-ji Temple
records.description: A Jodo-shu Buddhist temple founded in 1718 as a memorial to the monk Yuten of Zojoji; the surviving buildings date largely from 1724, and the main hall, main gate, and temple bell are registered national tangible cultural properties. Meguro City designated the temple a historic site in 1993.

tips.text: The temple grounds have long served as a resting place for Korean war dead, including remains repatriated to Japan after the 1945 sinking of the Ukishima Maru.

records.name: Otori Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine in Shimomeguro dedicated to the deities Yamato Takeru, Kuni-no-Tokotachi, and Ototachibanahime.

records.name: Himon'ya Hachiman Shrine
records.description: A Hachiman shrine in the Himonya district of Meguro, dedicated to the deities Ojin and Hachiman.

records.name: Nakameguro Hachiman Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine in Nakameguro dedicated to the deities Ojin and Hachiman.

records.name: Meguro Gajoen (Hyakudan Kaidan)
records.description: A historic banquet hall and hotel opened in 1931 by restaurateur Rikizo Hosokawa on the former Meiji-era estate of shipping magnate Shoichi Iwanaga. Its Hyakudan Kaidan ('hundred-step staircase'), a wooden corridor connecting seven ornately decorated banquet rooms, survives from the original building and is designated a Tokyo Tangible Cultural Property; the rest of the complex was rebuilt in an 85-billion-yen renovation completed in 1991.

tips.text: The Hyakudan Kaidan is only open to the public during periodic special exhibitions, not as a regular walk-in sight.

records.station: Meguro Station (JR Yamanote, Namboku, Mita, Meguro lines), about 3 minutes on foot

records.name: Meguro River
records.description: A 7.8 km river flowing through Setagaya, Meguro, and Shinagawa wards to Tokyo Bay. The stretch through Nakameguro is lined with more than a kilometer of cherry trees on both banks and is one of Tokyo's most popular hanami spots, with night illumination during peak bloom in late March/early April.

tips.text: The Nakameguro stretch is illuminated at night during the cherry blossom season, drawing large evening crowds.

records.station: Nakameguro Station (Tokyu Toyoko Line, Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)
records.address: 目黒川, 目黒区, 東京都, 日本

records.name: Nakameguro
records.description: A boutique- and cafe-filled neighborhood centered on the Meguro River, spanning five chome and covering about 0.9 sq km. The area name is often used loosely to include neighboring Kamimeguro, part of Aobadai, and Higashiyama.
records.station: Nakameguro Station (Tokyu Toyoko Line, Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line)
records.address: 中目黒, 上目黒三丁目, 上目黒, 目黒区, 東京都

records.name: Meguro Sky Garden
records.description: A 7,000 sq m looping rooftop garden built atop the Metropolitan Expressway's Ohashi Junction, rising 15-35 meters above street level with a 400 m circumference. It opened on March 30, 2013, is divided into planting zones, and includes a large lawn area (Opus Yume Hiroba).
records.station: Ikejiri-Ohashi Station (Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line), about 3 minutes on foot

records.name: Himonya Park
records.description: A 43,533 sq m ward park opened in 1933, centered on Himonya Pond (also called Benten Pond), a former irrigation reservoir. It has a children's animal corner with ponies, rabbits, and guinea pigs, pay boat rides on the pond, playgrounds, and sports facilities including a gymnasium and baseball field.
records.station: Gakugei-daigaku Station (Tokyu Toyoko Line), about 6 minutes on foot
records.address: 碑文谷公園, 碑文谷, 目黒区, 東京都, 日本

records.name: Komaba Park
records.description: A 40,400 sq m ward park created in 1975 on the former estate of the Maeda family. It contains the 1929 Tudor-style former Maeda residence, built for the 16th Marquis Toshinari Maeda with a Japanese-style garden annex added in 1930, as well as the Museum of Modern Japanese Literature.

tips.text: The former Maeda mansion was requisitioned by Allied occupation forces after WWII and used as a residence for U.S. Air Force and Army generals until 1957.

records.name: Saigoyama Park
records.description: A small hillside park in the Aobadai district named after Saigo Tsugumichi, younger brother of Saigo Takamori; it opened on May 28, 1981.
records.address: 西郷山公園, 青葉台二丁目, 青葉台, 目黒区, 東京都

records.name: Sugekari Park
records.description: A ward park in the Aobadai district of Meguro that opened on March 31, 2001.
records.address: 菅刈公園, 西郷山通り, 青葉台二丁目, 青葉台, 目黒区

records.name: Rinshi-no-mori Park
records.description: A park straddling Meguro and Shinagawa wards on the site of Japan's first national forestry experiment station, established in 1900. When the Forestry Agency relocated its research to Tsukuba, the land and its trees -- including 59 species from outside Japan -- were donated to Tokyo and opened to the public in 1989.

records.name: Komabano Park
records.description: A ward park in the Komaba district of Meguro that opened on March 31, 1986.

records.name: Japan Folk Crafts Museum (Nihon Mingeikan)
records.description: Founded in 1936 by philosopher and folk-craft advocate Soetsu Yanagi, this museum in Komaba preserves and exhibits mingei (folk crafts) -- Japanese and international handmade ceramics, textiles, and other everyday objects. The main building is a traditional Japanese-style structure with a black-tiled roof and a Registered Tangible Cultural Property; a 19th-century nagaya-mon gatehouse relocated from Tochigi Prefecture stands across the street.

tips.text: General admission is ¥1,500 for adults, ¥800 for high school students, and free for middle-school age and younger.
The separate West Building (Yanagi's former residence) is open only on the 2nd and 3rd Wednesdays and Saturdays of the month.

records.station: Komaba-Todaimae Station (Keio Inokashira Line), about 7 minutes on foot

records.name: Tokyo Photographic Art Museum
records.description: Opened in 1990 and moved to its current Yebisu Garden Place building in 1995, this was one of the first Japanese photography galleries not dedicated to a single photographer. It includes exhibition galleries, a movie theater, and a photography library, and adopted the nickname 'TOP Museum' in 2016.

tips.text: There is no entrance charge for the building itself; each exhibition has its own admission fee.

records.station: Ebisu Station (JR Yamanote Line, East Exit), about 7 minutes on foot
records.address: 1-13-3 Mita, Meguro City, Tokyo (inside Yebisu Garden Place)

records.name: Meguro Museum of Art, Tokyo
records.description: A ward art museum opened in November 1987 and designed by Nihon Sekkei. Its permanent collection includes works by Tsuguharu Fujita, Zenzaburo Kojima, Shikanosuke Oka, Kazuo Sakata, and Kumi Sugai; it holds no standing permanent exhibition, instead running a rotating program of shows.
records.hours: 10:00-18:00, Tuesday-Sunday and holidays (last entry 30 minutes before closing)
records.station: Meguro Station, about 10 minutes on foot

records.name: Meguro Parasitological Museum
records.description: A private research museum founded in 1953 by physician Satoru Kamegai to study parasitology and educate the public; it moved into its current six-story building in 1993. About 300 of its roughly 60,000 specimens are on display at a time, including an 8.8-meter tapeworm recovered from a patient.

tips.text: Admission is free, though the museum relies on donations since it receives no government funding.

records.station: Meguro Station (West Exit), about 12 minutes on foot

records.name: Meguro Persimmon Hall
records.description: A ward-run concert and performance arts venue in the Yakumo district of Meguro.

records.name: University of Tokyo, Komaba Campus
records.description: A campus of the University of Tokyo located in the Komaba district, adjacent to Komaba Park. It is known locally for a historic clock-tower building on its grounds.

records.name: Institute of Science Tokyo, Ookayama Campus
records.description: The main campus of the former Tokyo Institute of Technology, which merged with Tokyo Medical and Dental University in October 2024 to form the Institute of Science Tokyo. Two rows of cherry trees planted by graduates starting in 1950, especially in front of the Main Building, make the campus a local spring cherry-blossom viewing spot.

records.name: Gyoninzaka
records.description: A steep historic slope on the border of Shimomeguro and Kami-Osaki, associated with the Great Fire of Meiwa (1772) and running alongside Daien-ji temple.
records.address: 行人坂, 下目黒一丁目, 下目黒, 目黒区, 東京都
